name: Hexetidine

overview.mechanism: Evaluated as an antiseptic mouthrinse to reduce dental plaque and gingival inflammation; these clinical outcomes do not validate treatment of systemic infection [[HEX-2003,HEX-2005]].
uses: Mouthrinse use studied for plaque and gingivitis; verify local indications and formulation instructions [[HEX-2003,HEX-2005]].

evidence.title: Clinical evidence and limitations
evidence.intro: Study regimens are descriptions of research, not prescribing recommendations.

rows.design: Examiner-blind randomized controlled study; 134 adults completed two weeks.
rows.intervention: Hexetidine rinse, chlorhexidine positive control or hydroalcohol negative control; supervised rinsing as sole oral hygiene.
rows.findings: Compared with negative control, hexetidine reduced plaque, gingivitis and gingival bleeding indices.
rows.limitations: Short experimental model after dental prophylaxis, with usual mechanical hygiene withheld; does not establish replacement of routine oral care or long-term periodontal outcomes.

rows.design: Double-blind randomized study; 90 subjects; four weeks.
rows.findings: Active rinses improved plaque more than control, but between-group differences in bleeding and gingival inflammation were not significant. Hexetidine caused less discoloration than chlorhexidine.
rows.limitations: All groups improved. Within-group changes cannot be read as superiority for every dental endpoint.

sources.citation: Antiplaque and antigingivitis effectiveness of a hexetidine mouthwash. PubMed PMID: 12834495.
Clinical study on the effectiveness and side effects of hexetidine and chlorhexidine mouthrinses versus a negative control. PubMed PMID: 16161468.

draft_notes: Source-linked descriptive findings and safety information only. Current local product information, contraindications, formulation-specific dosing and renal schedules require verification.

revision_log.change: Added source-verified descriptive monograph, clinical evidence and safety limitations without unsupported dosing or inferred dialysis regimen.

common: Dental discoloration increased to some extent in all groups in the four-week trial; hexetidine did not differ significantly from negative control on the mean discoloration score [[HEX-2005]].

renal: These topical oral-care studies do not establish renal dose adjustment, dialysis use or safety of swallowed exposure. Product-specific restrictions remain to be verified [[HEX-2003,HEX-2005]].
